Adopt Shared Tooling's canonical validation cadence at exact published revision `4256171b5b7ec4c4cc4078548c1c1617ee150699` (0.12.5): focused checks for changed behavior and directly affected callers; full local suites remain reserved for an explicitly authorized release or an explicit request.

Refreshed on released Memory 0.39.0 through a normal merge without rewriting topic history. Only AGENTS.md and the active code-hygiene guide differ from main. Product source, dependency selections, package versions, executable snapshot and all other shared rules remain unchanged. Configured CI, required branch checks, release gates and separate runtime/effect authority are unchanged.

Validation at head 9179a5fdcf32f452c12c435e1956455dc2169afb: the exact published policy exists and its validation section was reviewed; all 26 local links in the changed documents exist; the expected two-file-only delta, instruction consistency and diff checks pass. No code suite was run for this documentation-only PR. Previous macOS failures were on its old dependency graph; fresh hosted checks must qualify this updated head. No merge or release was performed.

## Current publication blocker — 2026-10-20

[Testkit #88](https://github.com/dragginzgame/ic-testkit/pull/88) is refreshed at `5896f1888f6c00822289b03c1ce245c8ee7e94bf`; the optional IO child [#97](https://github.com/dragginzgame/ic-testkit/pull/97) is at `4c4c66b3dcfcba521dd36db73580c34cd12db599`. Both merge normally with current Testkit main 0.57.0 and retain Platform 0.2.1, Host 0.30, Wire 0.5, the renamed performance probe and unchanged own package metadata. Pending producer notes target 0.57.1. Both branches are mergeable; registry publication still blocks maintained Memory adoption.

Focused producer proof passes two allocator cases, four optional IO cases, strict package Clippy, actual Rust 1.91 native/Wasm checks, default graph isolation and verified packaging. The parent also passes substituted publication and complete isolated release-metadata/recovery checks. Fresh exact-head hosted native checks remain required; no producer merge or publication is claimed.

A temporary Memory 0.49.1 consumer against the exact Testkit source passes nine allocation/IO contract tests, all six explicit allocation measurement cases and strict native caller Clippy. Its 40 non-timing IO rows and eight allocation-diagnostic rows match the existing implementation. Current summary collection still allocates zero times; current detailed reports allocate once per call. These are native measurement contracts, not IC instruction/cycle or production Wasm savings.

The prospective patch is retained at `target/qualification/cleanup0492/native-adoption.patch`, with source identities beside it. It removes local allocator/observer implementation and cross-tree imports, preserves workloads/CSV/assertions, and rejects overflowed IO counts. The patch has no shipped path override or fabricated published lockfile: apply/select the real registry version and update the maintained lock only after publication. Memory's current helpers remain until then. Evidence: `/tmp/ic-memory-next3.us9qwuab/`.

---

Approved extraction under Testkit #86. The new ic-testkit-native package has no dependencies, measures only the selected thread and supports signed net bytes, nested-scope refusal and unwind cleanup. Prospective Memory adoption removes its allocator plumbing while retaining workloads, CSV output and exact assertions. Qualification preserves zero-allocation summaries and three-allocation detailed reports. Prepared patch: target/qualification/extractions0371/consumer-adoption.patch.
